sentences.text: Parvavis is an extinct enantiornithean bird known from the Upper Cretaceous of China. The fossil consists of a partially complete, articulated skeleton with skull fragments and feather impressions. Preserved skeletal elements include the tail, pygostyle, and the back of the skull. Parvavis was a small bird with a wingspan of approximately 15 centimeters.
A distinguishing feature of Parvavis is that the bottom joint of its second metatarsal is wider than the others. Parvavis possessed a reduced claw on its fourth toe.

Parvavis holds the distinction of being the first bird known from the Upper Cretaceous of China and the first Mesozoic bird from Southern China. At the time of its discovery, Parvavis was the only known Mesozoic bird from southern China.
Despite its small size, with a wingspan of approximately 15 centimeters, it represents a significant find for the region's avian history.
The skeleton of Parvavis was discovered near Luojumei in Yunnan province, China, in 2010. The holotype fossil was found in lake deposits within the Jiangdihe Formation.

The only known species, Parvavis chuxiongensis, was found in Luojumei Village, Chuxiong City, in southern China. Parvavis chuxiongensis was formally named and described in 2014 by Wang Min, Zhou Zhonghe, and Xu Guanghui.
The genus name Parvavis combines the Latin words for 'small' and 'bird'.

Bone structure analysis indicates the holotype individual was nearly fully grown when it died. Histological research suggests Parvavis reached near-adult size but remained unusually small for an enantiornithine.

Cladistic analyses place Parvavis in a basal position within the Enantiornithes, outside the Longipterygidae family. The basal position of Parvavis suggests that early enantiornithine forms existed for a longer period than previously thought.
Parvavis lived between 93.9 and 83.6 million years ago, during the Turonian to Santonian stages.
